summary: The note honors five retiring high school coaches during the 2023 fall season, each tied to a different school and sport. It recounts their years of service, achievements, and final games or meets in September and October 2023. It concludes that their influence on athletes and community will outlast their time on the sidelines.
one_line: Tribute to five retiring high school coaches in football, track, basketball, softball and soccer, marking farewells during the 2023 season.
key_facts: Coach James Harrison has coached football at Westfield High School for over 30 years and is known as the 'King of the Gridiron'.
Harrison led the Westfield Wolverines to three state championships and countless regional playoffs.
The Wolverines won on September 8, 2023, with past and present players gathering around Harrison after the game.
Coach Linda Thompson has had a 25-year career coaching track and field at Lincoln High School, nurturing numerous state champions and some national competitors.
Thompson's final meet was on September 15, when Lincoln secured another division title.
Coach Michael "Mike" Jensen has coached basketball at Central High School for 27 years, leading the Cougars to several regional titles.
Central High won on September 22 in a game that spotlighted Jensen.
Coach Angela Rodriguez has led Eastwood High softball for 20 years, winning state titles and earning a place in the hall of fame.
Rodriguez's tenure approached its final innings on September 29.
Coach David Lee has anchored Jackson High's soccer success for 22 years.
Lee's final match was held on October 6.
The note says the coaches built academic strongholds, fostered community spirit and equipped young people with skills for sports and life.
